JUSTIFICATION AND APPROVAL (J&A) FOR USE OF OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION

1. Contracting Activity:

Department of the Navy, Military Sealift Command (MSC), Prepositioning and Seabasing Program Office PM3/N105A.

2. Description of the Action Being Approved:

Award of a bridge contract for the Operation and Maintenance (O&M) of the governmentowned Expeditionary Transfer Dock (ESD) vessels on an other-than full-and-open-competition basis to the incumbent contractor, Ocean Ships, Inc. (OSI).

3. Description of Supplies/Services:

The original contract (N3220519C3003) and current bridge contract (N3220524C4127) provide for the worldwide O&M of ESD vessels, United States Naval Ship (USNS) JOHN GLENN and (USNS) MONTFORD POINT. The original contract was competitively procured and awarded to OSI on 28 January 2019. The current bridge contract consists of a one-year firm period and a 6month option which began on 02 November 2025 and is scheduled to conclude on 01 May 2026.

The period of performance will consist of a one-year firm period beginning 02 May 2026 to 01 May 2027. The requested 12 months is intended to cover the time needed to award a follow-on contract and conduct an adequate turnover. The period of performance has been structured to ensure continuity of operations during the completion of the competitive acquisition and transition to the new awardee, if applicable.

The bridge contract will be awarded as a firm-fixed-price contract with separately estimated pass-through expenses. The value of this J&A is [REDACTED] which is the estimated value of the fixed-price operating hire of this bridge contract. Funding for the fixed-price operating hire will be provided as follows:

J&A N3220526R0026 ESD Bridge These delays have impacted the Government's ability to transition to a new award by the current contract's end date.

The command acknowledges that other firms may be capable of providing these services under normal acquisition timelines. However, at this time, no other contractor could immediately assume full responsibility for all services currently being performed by the incumbent without resulting in unacceptable delays or potentially compromising the mission. Therefore, the criteria under RFO 6.103-1(c)(2) are met.

Awarding this bridge to a source other than the incumbent would result in substantial duplication of cost due to parallel mobilization, onboarding of qualified key shipboard and key shoreside staff, processing security clearances and redundant training. In addition, the current contract personnel have been integrated with NRL experiments for the past two and a half years and NRL would also incur additional costs due to the need to get new shipboard personnel up to speed with the current experiments. These costs would not be recoverable through competition, especially given the limited period of performance. There is insufficient time to develop, compete, evaluate, and award a short-term contract before a lapse in service would occur. Such a gap in service would severely disrupt NRL's critical national security mission activities that rely on the uninterrupted availability and specialized services of the ESD vessels.

The award of a competitive contract to the non-incumbent would result in the turnover of the ESD vessels, solely for the limited duration of this interim effort. This would be operationally burdensome, logistically complex, financially inefficient, and would likely require Government intervention to manage the safe and secure transition of assets between Operating Companies (OPCOs). [REDACTED] based on an estimated six-month operational turnover period. This estimate includes costs for both the incumbent and incoming contractors related to crew availability and support during turnover, and also includes additional costs due to delays of NRL's experiments. These costs do not include travel, lodging, material turnover, commodities, overtime or port and canal charges, and don't take into account the current mariner labor shortage, which could lengthen the turnover period. These [REDACTED] in non-recoverable expenses, which offer no long-term benefit to the Government and serve solely to enable a shortterm continuity of service, are not expected to be recovered by the Government through competition.

Furthermore, in the event of a transition between OPCOs, MSC would be required to assume responsibility for the safety and security of the vessels during turnover.
